# Fen

> A native Markdown editor for Mac, iPhone and iPad, written in Swift and SwiftUI. It turns your folders of plain `.md` files into a knowledge base you can search by meaning, link and ask. Answers cite their sources, every AI change goes through one gate and can be undone, and AI runs only through providers you add. Open source, Apple Silicon native. It grew out of a full rewrite of MacDown.

Fen is built and maintained by Zohar Babin (https://zoharbabin.com/), CSO at Kaltura, Inc. and a long-time open-source builder. Fen itself is not affiliated with Kaltura — it's an independent open-source project.

## What Fen is

- A rewrite of the original MacDown (Objective-C, by Tzu-ping Chung) in pure Swift and SwiftUI, sharing a cross-platform core (`FenCore`) between the macOS and iOS apps.
- Live Markdown preview with editor/preview scroll sync, syntax highlighting, MathJax, and Mermaid diagram rendering.
- GitHub-Flavored Markdown via Apple's swift-cmark (tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks, footnotes).
- An optional WYSIWYG-in-source live preview editing mode, a slash-command menu for inserting blocks, focus/typewriter mode, and synced line-number gutters between editor and preview.
- A Quick Look extension that renders `.md` files in Finder's preview panel, and a first-run sample document for new installs.
- Workspaces: add any number of folders, with or without git. Fen lists their notes without opening each file.
- On-device search by words and meaning (a model you download, EmbeddingGemma 2 or Qwen3 Embedding, covers 100+ languages), `[[wiki-links]]` with backlinks, related documents, and typed properties from a plain `schema.yaml`.
- Ask your workspaces: answers cite numbered sources with line numbers. Inline Ask AI and Enrich edit through one gate, and each edit can be undone.
- AI only through providers you add (Apple's on-device model, a Gemma 4 model you download, Ollama, or an OpenAI-compatible service). With none added, Fen makes no AI request.
- An opt-in MCP server on 127.0.0.1 (Mac), with per-client tokens and workspaces, and agent branches that leave your checkout alone.
- GitHub sync (clone, pull, push with a token limited to one repository), conflicts that wait for your choice, and version history that includes iCloud versions.
- iPhone and iPad: keyboard shortcuts, a share sheet in and out, and one pane at a time on a narrow screen.
- Free, MIT-licensed, no telemetry, no account required.
- Signed and notarized by Apple — installs without Gatekeeper warnings.

## Install

- Mac, download: `Fen.app.zip` from https://github.com/zoharbabin/fen/releases/latest. Needs macOS 15 or later.
- Mac, Homebrew: `brew tap zoharbabin/fen https://github.com/zoharbabin/fen` then `brew install --cask fen`.
- iPhone, iPad and the Mac App Store: in App Review. One listing will cover all three.
- From source: https://github.com/zoharbabin/fen#build-from-source

## Where Fen is headed

Shipped: the editor, export and the `fen-export` command, Quick Look, workspaces, search, wiki-links and backlinks, document types, Ask with sources, a write gate, an opt-in MCP server, GitHub sync, version history, iPhone and iPad support, signed and notarized builds, and a Homebrew cask. In review: the App Store release. Later: Live Preview parity (Experimental).
